diagrams.title: System context
diagrams.description: The browser uses the web proxy for REST and an authenticated API socket. Worker-owned shared dispatch feeds BullMQ; the activity consumer persists history and publishes invalidations. Clients never connect to the data stores.

diagrams.title: Package dependency boundaries
diagrams.description: Runtime imports flow from apps to packages. Shared jobs serves worker dispatch and API compatibility seams; OpenAPI-to-API is build-only. Contracts remain framework-free.

diagrams.title: Core data relationships
diagrams.description: This selected relationship map emphasizes tenant keys and task/activity links. It omits refresh sessions, invitations, grants, status overrides and seed metadata; the full schema and all audit timestamps remain in the database reference. Owner references on field definitions are polymorphic, not an implied Node foreign key.

diagrams.title: Contract to generated client
diagrams.description: One contract feeds server DTOs and client generation. Spec export uses isolated providers rather than connecting to production data. Generated transport operations are not handwritten in UI components.

diagrams.title: Login and session issuance
diagrams.description: Passwords are verified server-side. The access token is short-lived and held in memory; the refresh credential is stored as a digest and transported in an HttpOnly cookie.

diagrams.title: Refresh rotation and replay
diagrams.description: Concurrent requests share refresh coordination. Credential replay revokes the family, and retrying is bounded. Workspace changes use their typed, membership-checked operation and clear old scoped client state.

diagrams.title: Ancestor permission decision
diagrams.description: A child allow cannot bypass a denied or unallowed private ancestor. Visibility permits member task editing, while container/configuration/grant administration remains admin-only.

diagrams.title: Request and tenant boundary
diagrams.description: Authentication establishes identity; tenant repositories enforce data scoping. Writes recheck mutable authority and configuration under the lock. Foreign-tenant identifiers do not become authority and return not-found behavior.

diagrams.title: Scoped status resolution
diagrams.description: Child rows patch display/visibility attributes, not the canonical status identity or category. A nearer explicit visible override can restore a hidden status. Sibling lists can therefore resolve different sets safely.

diagrams.title: Field resolution and value validation
diagrams.description: Field overrides replace complete definitions, including options and requiredness. Unknown keys and invalid options fail. Clearing a required value still fails final validation.

diagrams.title: Safe configuration mutation
diagrams.description: A deletion can reveal inherited configuration, so validation checks the result across descendants. In-use statuses/fields cannot leave tasks with an invalid board or schema.

diagrams.title: Atomic cross-list move
diagrams.description: A move either commits completely or leaves the task unchanged. Source-only custom values are not silently discarded; the payload must clear them and supply required destination values.

diagrams.title: Ordering and no-op handling
diagrams.description: Reordering may change sibling positions as well as the dragged task. Only changed rows receive version updates, and a canonical no-op does not create history.

diagrams.title: UI composition ownership
diagrams.description: Reusable presentation stays in the UI package; form bindings stay in forms. Web coordinates generated operations, permissions, URL state and feature interactions.

diagrams.title: Load a consistent board
diagrams.description: Statuses and fields begin concurrently; validated statuses determine the first task request for each column. The complete bundle must have compatible versions before rendering, including empty resolved columns.

diagrams.title: Optimistic drag lifecycle
diagrams.description: Optimistic state is a temporary task/list projection. Settlement removes that projection and refetches authoritative lists; failure repairs its own preview while preserving newer changes. Keyboard and explicit move controls share the server operation.

diagrams.title: Form submit and recovery
diagrams.description: Local invalid input does not trigger a success request/toast. Server failures preserve the draft, and conflicts never silently replace an edit with another client’s data.

diagrams.title: Redis roles
diagrams.description: Redis is not a task or resolved-configuration cache. Its counter, queue, publication and adapter responsibilities are separate; environment isolation must cover all of them.

diagrams.title: Status change to activity and invalidation
diagrams.description: The request succeeds after database commit, independently of asynchronous activity. The worker reaches browsers through the gateway; it never bypasses recipient authorization.

diagrams.title: Outbox state and lease recovery
diagrams.description: The worker can claim before the dispatcher marks the event queued, so this is not a strict linear chain. Token-checked updates stop stale claimants from overwriting newer state. Failed means quarantine, not an automatic success.

diagrams.title: Retry and duplicate safety
diagrams.description: Stable event IDs and idempotent activity support at-least-once delivery. Repeated publication is possible, and disconnected clients recover by reading current authorized state.

diagrams.title: Authorized socket delivery
diagrams.description: Room membership is a routing aid, not durable authorization. Periodic and emission-time checks prevent revoked users from continuing to receive protected updates.

diagrams.title: Trunk and review flow
diagrams.description: This is the documented operating model. CI runs today; branch protection and merge policy are repository settings that must be configured and verified separately.

diagrams.title: Eight CI lanes and release gates
diagrams.description: Five workspace checks, UI tests and two Compose checks start independently. Main publication targets GHCR; protected settings gate the temporary Vercel source deployment.

diagrams.title: Independent release decision
diagrams.description: The first published version initializes at 0.1.0. Later release ownership comes from files and dependency fingerprints, not just commit scope text. Complete reverts can produce no release; changing API internals alone need not release the browser.

diagrams.title: Publication identity and retry
diagrams.description: Publication checks its committed source and per-app history. It may publish an earlier queued main commit; the deployment layer separately rejects stale workflow-main identities.

diagrams.title: One image with different runtime configuration
diagrams.status: Runtime seams implemented; ECR and promotion planned
diagrams.description: Runtime configuration seams and current GHCR publication exist. ECR integration and ordered unchanged-image promotion remain planned, with isolated data and Redis per environment.

diagrams.title: Temporary Vercel demo topology
diagrams.description: The temporary demo routes public pages/REST to web and Socket.IO to API; web uses the private binding. Neon, Upstash TLS Redis and the worker daemon were exercised in P38-03. This is not future ECR production.

diagrams.title: Demo verification and remaining gates
diagrams.description: P38 implementation and manual live checks are complete. Protected main-branch CD activation remains separate; ECR publication and unchanged-image promotion are future work.

diagrams.title: Selected-candidate promotion
diagrams.description: The planned ECR promoter pins selected app digests, updates only changed image/configuration states and retains unselected services in every environment. New main commits never replace an in-flight candidate; compatibility and runtime settings are checked at each target.
